hints.title: Sign Inversion Propagation
hints.text: Multiplying any two adjacent elements by -1 allows moving negative signs freely across any path on the grid.

hints.title: Parity of Negative Numbers
hints.text: If the total count of negative numbers is even, all values in the matrix can be made non-negative.

hints.title: Isolating the Minimal Absolute Value
hints.text: If the negative count is odd, exactly one number must retain a negative sign; choose the element with smallest absolute value.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: matrix row and column dimensions
complexity.notes: Single pass matrix reduction checking negative parity and minimal magnitude.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph search or backtracking over sign flips is intractable on N x N matrices.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency graph connectivity guarantees arbitrary pair cancellations in O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should deduce that negative count parity dictates whether all numbers become positive.
